Now I have a complete picture. Let me compile the full analysis. --- ## Deep Analysis: Image Presentation on the Original Squarespace Site vs. New Next.js Site ### Summary of Findings **The original Squarespace site displays ALL images at their natural/intrinsic aspect ratios. The new Next.js site force-crops every single image with `object-fit: cover` inside fixed-pixel-height containers. This is a fundamental difference that is likely destroying the composition of carefully designed portfolio pieces.** --- ### Original Squarespace Site -- How Images Are Actually Presented #### Homepage (jaimeibrahim.com/) - **Layout:** Squarespace's 24-column CSS grid (desktop), 8-column (mobile) - **Max width:** 1500px with 4vw side gutters - **Image rendering:** Images are placed inside grid cells that use `auto` row heights. There is **no `object-fit` property applied anywhere**. Images scale to 100% of their container width, and their height is determined by the image's natural aspect ratio. - **Thumbnails:** Project thumbnails are contained within margins (not edge-to-edge), with 11px gaps between grid cells. Each thumbnail respects its own natural proportions. - **Key fact:** The grid uses `grid-template-rows: repeat(N, minmax(calc(var(--container-width) * var(--row-height-scaling-factor)), auto))` -- the `auto` keyword is critical. It means rows grow to fit the natural image height. #### Battle Bank (/work/battlebank) - **8 images** displayed in a responsive grid layout - **No `object-fit: cover`** detected anywhere in the CSS - **Container heights:** All `auto` -- determined by the image's intrinsic dimensions, not forced pixel values - **Layout:** Mixed positioning within a 24-column desktop grid. Some images appear side-by-side through grid column allocation (e.g., grid columns 2-14 and 14-26), but each image retains its natural aspect ratio - **Spacing:** 11px consistent gap between grid cells - **Images span full container width** of their grid cells, with height determined naturally - **Result:** Logo marks, product mockups, app screens, and debit card designs all render at their designed proportions #### GLG Brand Identity (/work/glgbrand) - **9 images** in a vertical-scroll layout - **Single-column dominant** with staggered positioning across the grid for visual rhythm - **No `object-fit`** declarations - **Natural aspect ratios** preserved -- images size responsively through their grid containers - **Spacing:** 11px gap within the grid system - **Max width:** 1500px #### LiquidStock (/work/liquidstock) - **4 images** in a **single-column vertical stack** - **No side-by-side pairing** -- each image occupies its own full-width block - **Container heights:** `auto` -- no fixed dimensions - **Natural aspect ratios** -- the logo, mockup, animated GIF, and brochure layout each display at their designed proportions - **Spacing:** 11px row gap #### The Year Ahead (/work/yearahead) - **7 images** in a vertical flow - **Single-column layout** on mobile; multi-column grid on desktop - **No fixed-height containers** -- rows use `minmax()` with `auto` - **Natural aspect ratios** preserved - **Spacing:** 11px on mobile, 0px on some desktop sections - **Flow:** Logo -> description -> branded assets in sequence #### TIAA Branding (/work/tiaa-branding) - **5 images** in a grid layout - **One notable side-by-side pair** on desktop: heritage wall images positioned at grid columns 3-17 and 14-26 (overlapping column range creates a visual pair) - **No `object-fit`** anywhere - **Container heights:** `auto` -- adapts to image content - **Natural aspect ratios** maintained throughout #### Construction Wall (/work/construction) - **5 images** in a **pure single-column vertical stack** - **No side-by-side images at all** - **All images full-width** of their container - **Container heights:** auto, determined by content - **Natural aspect ratios** -- documentary-style construction photos displayed without any cropping #### Event Brand (/work/eventbrand) - **6 images** in a vertical sequence - **Single-column** on mobile; multi-column grid on desktop - **No `object-fit`** declarations found - **Container heights:** auto - **Natural aspect ratios** preserved - **Flow:** Moodboard -> logo -> color variations -> applications -> photography -> compositions --- ### Common Patterns Across ALL Original Pages | Property | Original Squarespace Site | |----------|--------------------------| | `object-fit` | **Not used anywhere** | | Container heights | **`auto`** -- adapts to image content | | Aspect ratios | **Natural/intrinsic** -- never force-cropped | | Layout | Predominantly **single-column vertical stacks** | | Side-by-side pairs | Rare (only TIAA and Battle Bank have some) | | Spacing | **11px** consistent gap | | Max width | **1500px** | | Side gutters | **4vw** desktop, **6vw** mobile | | Image width | **100% of container** (responsive) | | Image delivery | Squarespace CDN with `?format=1500w` responsive sizing | --- ### New Next.js Site -- What Is Different (and Problematic) Here is every instance of `object-fit: cover` with a fixed-height container in the current codebase: #### 1. GridCard.tsx (homepage + work page thumbnails) File: `C:\Users\User\JaimeIbrahim\src\components\GridCard.tsx`, lines 27-34: ```tsx
``` The `height` prop is a **fixed pixel value** passed from `GRID_ROWS_HOME` / `GRID_ROWS_ALL` (e.g., 560px, 520px, 380px, 400px, 480px, 460px, 340px). Combined with `fill` + `objectFit: "cover"`, this **crops images to fit these arbitrary containers**. #### 2. Project Detail Hero (`/work/[slug]/page.tsx`), line 79: ```tsx
``` Fixed height container (`clamp(300px, 50vh, 600px)`) with `object-fit: cover`. **Crops the hero image.** #### 3. Project Detail Gallery (same file, lines 108-113): ```tsx
``` **Every detail image** is forced into a fixed pixel height (440, 300, 320, or 460px) and cropped with `object-fit: cover`. #### 4. CaseStudySection.tsx (lines 50-51, 69-70, 81-82, 99-100): ```tsx // Single image sections:
// Paired image sections:
// h = 300 or 400
// Triple image sections:
// h = 280 or 380
``` **Every single image** in every case study section is cropped. --- ### Side-by-Side Comparison | Property | Original (Squarespace) | New (Next.js) | |----------|----------------------|---------------| | `object-fit` | **None** | `cover` on **every image** | | Container heights | **`auto`** (image dictates) | **Fixed px** (300-560px) | | Image cropping | **Never** | **Always** | | Layout pattern | Mostly **single column** stacks | **Asymmetric grid pairs** (2fr/1fr) | | Side-by-side pairs | Rare, only via grid positioning | **Forced on every page** | | Image proportions | **Preserved** | **Destroyed** | | Max width | 1500px | 1400px | --- ### The Core Problem The original Squarespace portfolio presents images as designed pieces -- each one at its natural aspect ratio, flowing vertically down the page in a simple, clean layout. A landscape logo presentation gets wide and short. A tall app mockup gets narrow and tall. A square brand element stays square. The new Next.js site forces every image into pre-defined height containers (560px, 480px, 440px, 380px, etc.) and uses `object-fit: cover` to fill those containers, which **crops off portions of every image**. For portfolio work -- where each image is a carefully composed design piece -- this destroys the visual integrity of the work being showcased. Additionally, the original site's project pages are predominantly **single-column vertical stacks** (images flowing one after another, full width), while the new site forces images into **asymmetric grid pairs** (2fr/1fr alternating). This is a layout decision from the Gretel-inspired design system that may not serve the actual content -- especially for projects like Construction Wall (5 documentary photos that are simply stacked vertically on the original) or LiquidStock (4 images in a pure single column). ### Recommendation To match the original site's approach, images should: 1. Use `width` + `height` attributes (or `width: "100%"` + `height: "auto"`) instead of `fill` + `object-fit: cover` 2. Let image containers have `auto` height so images render at their natural aspect ratio 3. Default to single-column layouts for project detail pages, unless the project specifically benefits from side-by-side presentation 4. Reserve the asymmetric grid system for the homepage thumbnail grid (where controlled cropping for visual rhythm is an intentional editorial choice), but even there, consider whether natural proportions would be better
